title: Perhaps Not The Answer You Were Expecting But You Asked For It
byline: Conor McBride · “an accidental blook” of Stack Overflow answers, October 2019
note: A compilation of Stack Overflow answers grouped by theme. Each section is one answer, listed under the question it answers; only the chapters are summarized. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: Conor McBride (“pigworker” on Stack Overflow) collected his answers into a book. Read in sequence they form an unusual course in typed functional programming: Haskell’s corners, recursion schemes, applicative functors and why they compose when monads do not, the calculus of datatypes (derivatives as one-hole contexts, zippers and comonads), dependently typed programming in Haskell with GADTs, singletons and type families, and finally type theory itself. The tone is playful and the arguments are precise.
